top.title: Clemson players highlight ‘Support Swinney’ sign after beating Duke
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images Clemson players highlight ‘Support Swinney’ sign after beating Duke appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Clemson Tigers heard the outside noise all week, and they answered it with a statement win for head coach Dabo Swinney on his 57th birthday. Following Friday night’s 20-10 road upset over the Duke Blue Devils in Durham, N.C., Clemson players rallied on the sideline to hold up a fan-made “Support Swinney” poster while chanting “Dabo” and singing “Happy Birthday.” Offensive linemen Harris Sewell and Grant Wise led the postgame tribute after a turbulent week in which critics questioned Swinney’s program following a loss to the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets and his bold national title guarantee. Instead of folding as double-digit underdogs, the Tigers dominated the trenches to improve to 7-4 overall and 5-3 in ACC play. ‘Support Swinney’ sign and ‘Dabo’ chant making their way into Clemson’s postgame celebrations @ClemsonFB beats Duke 20-10 pic.twitter.com/GTLbQtlfOb Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Caroline Soro (@caroline_soro) November 21, 2026 Clemson controlled the clock for 37:15 and piled up 384 total yards behind a ground-and-pound attack that churned out 220 rushing yards. Making his first career start, third-string quarterback Trent Pearman efficiently managed the offense, completing 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards without a turnover while adding 51 rushing yards and a 9-yard touchdown run on six carries. Wide receiver-turned-quarterback Chris Denson also punished Duke’s front with 71 yards and a 7-yard fourth-quarter score on 16 rushes, while running back Jarvis Green paced the backfield with 84 yards on 16 carries. Wideout T.J. Moore hauled in four catches for 68 yards, and kicker Nolan Hauser drilled field goals from 36 and 39 yards. On the other side of the ball, Clemson’s defense smothered Duke, limiting the Blue Devils to 247 yards and 11 first downs. Linebacker Fletcher Cothran recorded a sack, and safety Corey Myrick sealed the momentum with an interception against Duke quarterback Walker Eget, who went 16 of 38 for 149 yards. Aside from running back Nate Sheppard’s 116 rushing yards and 55-yard touchdown burst, Duke found zero room to breathe. Critics may still doubt Clemson’s ceiling, but inside that locker room, the Tigers clearly have Swinney’s back. top.title: Oregon kicker Gage Hurych scores on trick-play run
top.description: EAST LANSING, Mich. – If style and flash are what the College Football Playoff ranking committee wants to see from teams contending for the postseason, Oregon obliged Oct. 20 at Michigan State. The No. 13 Ducks put together a performance that included another highlight-reel touchdown catch from star receiver Dakorien Moore, a breakout performance from third-string running back Brandon Smith, a stingy, two-takeaway effort by the defense, and oh yeah, a touchdown run by their kicker on a fake field-goal attempt. Gage Hurych, the former standout lacrosse player from West Linn High School, scored on a 15-yard run at the end of the first half to ignite Oregon’s 45-7 win against Michigan State Friday night at Spartan Stadium. It was the fourth straight win for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten Conference), who continue their late-season push to make the CFP. “We knew that we had to be able to take advantage of opportunities to be able to go out there and score,” Oregon’s Dan Lanning said. “I think once we kind of figured that out it allowed us to go out there and show what I think we are, which is one of the best teams here down the stretch.” Hurych’s score – a play three seasons in the making – electrified the Oregon sideline and ignited the Ducks after an otherwise sluggish first half. With seven seconds to go before halftime, the Ducks lined up for a 35-yard field-goal attempt. But instead, holder Bailey Ettridge took the snap and flipped it to Hurych, who ran to his left, shook off one attempted tackle and dove into the end zone. The Oregon sidelined erupted in celebration after the play. “Coach Lanning about punched the air out of me when (Hurych) he scored,” quarterback Dylan Raiola said. “It definitely did get the guys going,” beamed Hurych, a junior in his first season as the Ducks’ primary kicker. “I mean, guys have seen that in practice for literally three years. I think everybody’s been waiting for that call to go for it.” The play was reviewed, as it appeared Hurych’s right leg might have hit the ground at the 1-yard line before he crossed into the end zone. But the call on the field stood and Oregon took a 17-0 lead into halftime. “My knee didn’t touch the ground, for the record,” said Hurych, who became the first Oregon kicker to rush for a touchdown since Paul Martinez on Sept. 9, 2006 versus Fresno State. “I’m glad it was at the 15-yard line and not the 16,” Lanning joked. “Gage just said if we ever call it, I’m going to score and he did that today.” Hurych’s touchdown was the highlight, but the entire scoring drive was impressive, considering that when it began with 1:41 to play in the half, the Ducks had only 92 yards of offense. top.description: ‘Too many avoidable goals’: Maresca warns Manchester City to tighten up at the back Enzo Maresca has said Manchester City must stop conceding 'avoidable goals' as the club look to end their winless run. Manchester City headed into the international break on a run of three consecutive Premier League defeats. The Cityzens lost to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in succession, to fall six points adrift of Arsenal in the title race. Defensive lapses have been evident, while goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma has faced scrutiny for his performances. Speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Fulham this afternoon, Maresca warned his side that they must tighten up defensively. "I was not thinking we were doing everything well when we were winning games. I’m not thinking we did everything wrong when we lost games," he said. "There are things we need to do better and no doubt we will do better. "We are conceding too many goals. Most of them are avoidable. So we need to avoid mistakes and try to deal with it [better] when it happens." top.title: Luka Doncic, Walker Kessler React To JJ Redick’s Fiery Locker Room Outburst In Lakers’ Comeback Win vs. Kings
top.description: LOS ANGELES, CA - NOVEMBER 20: Walker Kessler #14, Luka Doncic #77, and Head Coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers talk during the game against the Sacramento Kings during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on November 20, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images) The Lakers fought back from an 11-point third-quarter deficit to steal a 106-104 win over the Kings tonight, despite not playing their best on both ends of the floor early. After the game, JJ Redick was asked how he managed to rally the troops and motivate the Lakers at halftime, when they headed to the locker room down by eight points. “I feel like I did a decent job of regulating [team emotions] at halftime; they may have a different opinion of that. I can’t repeat every word I used, but the main message was we got to be tougher; we got to bring a little bit of energy,” JJ Redick said at his postgame press conference. Luka Doncic and Walker Kessler recalled the incident differently, but the team took the message maturely instead of getting in their feelings about what JJ Redick said. “Yeah, I mean, he yells. I’m used to it,” Luka Doncic said as the room broke out into laughter. “But it got us all fired up. So sometimes it’s good to hear.” Luka Doncic had a rough night from behind the three-point line, especially. He finished with 25 points, eight assists, four rebounds, and two steals, shooting 9-18 from the field (50.0% FG) and 2-9 from beyond the arc (22.2% 3P). Doncic sat out most of the fourth quarter and took only one field-goal attempt in the five minutes he played. The Lakers needed their other players to step up as the defense kept swarming the Slovenian superstar. In a game where Zach LaVine missed a good look for a game-winner at the final buzzer, Walker Kessler missed two crucial free throws that could have put the game out of the Kings’ reach before the final possession. Walker Kessler also had a relatively slow night, scoring just six of his 15 points in the first half. He finished with 15 points, seven rebounds, two assists, three blocks, and one steal while shooting 7-11 from the field (63.6% FG). Kessler suggested that some of Redick’s halftime outburst in the locker room was directed at him. “He lit me up a little bit. Rightfully so,” said Kessler on JJ Redick’s message to the team at halftime. “It was constructive. He was like, ‘I know you can do this. Do it,’” Kessler explained . Sometimes, nights like this remind you of the fierce competition and excess of talent in the league, and how even a bottom team like the Kings is testing the nerves of a playoff contender like the Lakers. Fortunately, the Lakers somehow held on to the lead they gained down the stretch and came away with the win. Otherwise, JJ Redick may have had another outburst at the team after the final buzzer. top.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
top.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance than in Mexico when I was on the front row. "Kimi did a great job and he probably thought it wasn't going to work out so well being so close but with the tow it worked out." Ferguson famously pledged to knock Liverpool off their perch and made good on those desires. The modern-day United are scrambling around on the bottom of the cage, flapping about in the muck of 18th position in the Premier League. That is an unfathomably low ebb for the dominant club of the Premier League era, but every manager since Ferguson has measured up poorly. Pochettino will begin the work of snapping that long sequence as Merseyside bays for Mancunian blood on Sunday. That passage of time is perhaps on the Argentine's side. top.title: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find
top.description: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find Ao Tanaka is a man of few words but a man of many skills, says his boss. The 28-year-old's taciturn nature was portrayed perfectly by a recent interaction with a former colleague on international duty. Japan's fixture with Brazil handed Tanaka a reunion with Lucas Perri, who is out on loan this season with Torino in Serie A. Farke was keen to find out how the pair got on, so asked his midfielder. "Everyone seems to speak about Ao Tanaka," said Farke. "The only one who never seems to speak is Ao Tanaka himself. So we had a short conversation about how it was for him to see Lucas Perri in the game against Brazil. Ao said, 'I said hello...and goodbye. That's it.' So this is how Ao Tanaka is. So he is not a man of many words, but of many skills on the football pitch. And we all love him." His form of late has attracted praise. And numbers back it up. No midfielder in the Premier League presses passing lanes more than Tanaka, who is Leeds' best tackler on Gradient Sports data. What Farke has seen in his midfielder is a level of consistency that was difficult to acquire as he found his feet in the Premier League. "It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship," said Farke. "Last season was his first year in the top league, Premier League level. I think he had also shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of this consistency. And I would also agree that he is finding this during the season. "So it was not always a 10 out of 10 performance, but I think it's important for a player once you're mature that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10. And this is what he's doing. So on perhaps even the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team and also against the ball." Tanaka's tackling prowess is also borne out by data. Gradient say only two players in the Premier League win more tackles per 90 minutes than the Japan international. That's an area in which he has pleased his boss, who still wants more. "Strong in the duels, still sometimes decision-making and in front of the goal he can be a bit calmer," said Farke. "But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment."

The outlet assures that the Manchester City defender had emerged as the most convincing candidate for Hansi Flick, but his preference to remain in England prevented the Catalan club from pursuing the deal further. It is understood that Barcelona assessed several defensive options throughout the summer transfer window but could not find an alternative that received sufficient approval from both the coaching staff and the sporting department. This is because despite the underlying need, the club did not want to sign a player just for the sake of it. top.title: Rising star to play at World Darts Championship
top.description: Henry Coates will make his debut at the PDC World Darts Championships in December [PDC] A rising darts star is set to make his dreams a reality by playing at this year's World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace. Henry Coates, 20, secured his place in December's tournament after a breakthrough year which saw him become only the fifth player to win a Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) ranking title without a tour card . Coates, from Matlock, Derbyshire, also narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen during his "incredible" Grand Slam of Darts debut on Saturday. He qualified for the worlds by being a top player on the Challenge Tour Order of Merit rankings , determined by prize money won during the year. "The way that some of the results have gone in my favour means that I'm going to be playing at Ally Pally in December," said Coates. "I'm going to achieve my dream of playing there." Coates narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen [PDC] Coates, who began playing darts when he was two, secured his qualification for the Grand Slam of Darts by winning his PDC ranking title in the summer. Being from a fifth generation family of butchers, with a shop in Darley Dale, Coates said it was "incredible" to make his debut in the televised competition. The debutant held his own against Van Gerwen but the three-time champion won the deciding leg to clinch a 5-4 win. Despite the close defeat, Coates ended his first Grand Slam on a high with a "better" 5-4 victory over Sweden's Jeffrey de Graaf. "I loved every minute of it. I played so well, even the crowd were chanting my name," he said. He said his phone had been buzzing "non-stop" with messages about his performance during his Grand Slam debut. Parents, Tanya and Nick said watching their son go from playing on a magnetic dartboard while still in nappies to competing against some of the best players in the world "still feels like a dream". His father admitted he still gets nervous watching his son play on the big stage. "I pace about and I have to turn it off because I want him to win and do well," he said. The PDC World Darts Championship, which takes place between 11 December and 3 January, sees a total of 128 players competing to become world champion and claim £1m prize money. This year's event will be held in the Alexandra Palace's Great Hall, for the first time, meaning new attendance records will be set. With his opponents for the tournament still yet to be revealed, Coates hopes a good performance event will take his career to even greater heights. top.title: Max Verstappen responds to George Russell after Vegas clash
top.description: Motorsport photo During the final practice session for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen and George Russell crossed paths once again. The Dutchman overtook the Mercedes driver, but then slowed down in front of him and, according to the stewards, changed direction several times. Russell subsequently went down the inside of the four-time world champion, leading to contact between the two at Turn 14. It earned both rivals a trip to the stewards, although they ultimately dealt with the incident by issuing a warning. Unlike a reprimand, a warning carries no consequences at all. When Verstappen was asked about the incident during the press conference after qualifying, the Dutchman had little interest in discussing it. Asked what had happened, he simply replied: "Nothing. Nothing happened." Russell, however, subsequently launched a scathing attack on the Red Bull driver in the media pen. Speaking to Sky Sports Italy, Russell said, among other things: "I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy." Verstappen was largely unmoved. When Motorsport.com asked him about the clash during the Dutch media session that followed in the Las Vegas paddock, he replied: "I don't even want to waste my time on that. It's not worth it to me at all." top.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
top.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. top.title: Lakers’ win over Kings fueled by JJ Redick’s halftime speech
top.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) celebrates a made three from his assist during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Friday November 20th, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES — Walker Kessler picked up three fouls before halftime, and the Lakers went to the locker room down eight to a one-win Sacramento team. JJ Redick had a message for the group and a more pointed one for his starting center. “We got to be tougher, we got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick said of his halftime message. “He definitely lit into me and it was good,” Kessler said. “I needed it. That’s what makes a good coach.” Kessler helped the Lakers erase an 11-point third-quarter deficit, and Quentin Grimes hit a step-back 3-pointer with 56.3 seconds remaining to lift Los Angeles to a 106-104 win over the Kings on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers improved to 14-3 overall and 2-1 in NBA Cup West Group C, picking up their 10th win in 11 games and ending a homestand that had them play three games in a four-day span. Luka Dončić, who led the Lakers with 25 points and eight assists, was asked whether Redick’s halftime talk was more than a talk, which is how Redick put it after the game. “Yeah, I mean, he yells. I’m used to it,” Dončić said. “But it got us all fired up. So sometimes it’s good to hear.” The response took a few possessions. Sacramento stretched its lead to 67-56 early in the third quarter, but Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed two offensive rebounds in the period and threw down a dunk that brought the Lakers within two heading into the fourth. Kessler gave L.A. the lead 18 seconds into the final quarter with his first 3-pointer as a Laker. He later broke an 89-89 tie with a cutting layup off a pass from Collin Sexton, who scored six points in the first five minutes of the quarter. Kessler finished with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks. Matisse Thybulle added 14 points on 4-for-5 shooting from beyond the arc and set up Grimes for the deciding shot. The Lakers led by eight with 4:50 left before the Kings tied it twice. De’Andre Hunter, who scored a game-high 30 points, made a driving bank shot to even the score at 103 before Grimes hit his only 3-pointer of the night. Zach LaVine made one of two free throws to bring Sacramento within two and Kessler missed both of his attempts with 5.3 seconds left which gave the Kings a last chance shot on the final possession from LaVine. LaVine’s potential game-winning 3-pointer hit from the rim at the buzzer that crushed any possibility of sending fans heartbroken. Grimes finished with 13 points and seven assists. Austin Reaves missed his fourth consecutive game with a left heel bruise, and the Lakers will host Utah again Monday at 7 p.m. PT.

top.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
top.description: Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. nigeria.title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company. It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music. For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning. Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history. She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship. Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife. The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again. Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France. It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring. Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down. nigeria.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
nigeria.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. nigeria.title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
nigeria.description: By Shola Ogundipe Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women. The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex. Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes. The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women. Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue. What emerged was an unexpected picture. The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions. The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity. “Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health. But perhaps the most striking finding was the difference between male and female mice. Female mice had a population of eosinophils that appeared to work more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells found in fat tissue. Their cooperation seemed to support a healthier environment within fat tissue and better metabolic function. Male mice, however, showed a different response when exposed to a high-fat diet. For twenty years, the union between Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and Zainab Musa Kwankwaso appeared to demonstrate that bloodline and political loyalty could coexist under one roof. Today, that roof has given way. The breakdown of the marriage between Governor Yusuf and Zainab, niece of his estranged political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and raised in the former governor’s household, is more than a headline from Government House. It raises an uncomfortable question: what happens when the political alliance connecting two families collapses, but the marriage binding them is left caught in its aftermath? Sometimes, they are reinforced through family connections. nigeria.description: By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing. In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard. They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things. A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count. In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation. Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. sports.title: Oregon kicker Gage Hurych scores on trick-play run
sports.description: EAST LANSING, Mich. – If style and flash are what the College Football Playoff ranking committee wants to see from teams contending for the postseason, Oregon obliged Oct. 20 at Michigan State. The No. 13 Ducks put together a performance that included another highlight-reel touchdown catch from star receiver Dakorien Moore, a breakout performance from third-string running back Brandon Smith, a stingy, two-takeaway effort by the defense, and oh yeah, a touchdown run by their kicker on a fake field-goal attempt. Gage Hurych, the former standout lacrosse player from West Linn High School, scored on a 15-yard run at the end of the first half to ignite Oregon’s 45-7 win against Michigan State Friday night at Spartan Stadium. It was the fourth straight win for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten Conference), who continue their late-season push to make the CFP. “We knew that we had to be able to take advantage of opportunities to be able to go out there and score,” Oregon’s Dan Lanning said. “I think once we kind of figured that out it allowed us to go out there and show what I think we are, which is one of the best teams here down the stretch.” Hurych’s score – a play three seasons in the making – electrified the Oregon sideline and ignited the Ducks after an otherwise sluggish first half. With seven seconds to go before halftime, the Ducks lined up for a 35-yard field-goal attempt. But instead, holder Bailey Ettridge took the snap and flipped it to Hurych, who ran to his left, shook off one attempted tackle and dove into the end zone. The Oregon sidelined erupted in celebration after the play. “Coach Lanning about punched the air out of me when (Hurych) he scored,” quarterback Dylan Raiola said. “It definitely did get the guys going,” beamed Hurych, a junior in his first season as the Ducks’ primary kicker. “I mean, guys have seen that in practice for literally three years. I think everybody’s been waiting for that call to go for it.” The play was reviewed, as it appeared Hurych’s right leg might have hit the ground at the 1-yard line before he crossed into the end zone. But the call on the field stood and Oregon took a 17-0 lead into halftime. “My knee didn’t touch the ground, for the record,” said Hurych, who became the first Oregon kicker to rush for a touchdown since Paul Martinez on Sept. 9, 2006 versus Fresno State. “I’m glad it was at the 15-yard line and not the 16,” Lanning joked. “Gage just said if we ever call it, I’m going to score and he did that today.” Hurych’s touchdown was the highlight, but the entire scoring drive was impressive, considering that when it began with 1:41 to play in the half, the Ducks had only 92 yards of offense. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. sports.title: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find
sports.description: Ao Tanaka's four-word Brazil reunion and the missing piece he's started to find Ao Tanaka is a man of few words but a man of many skills, says his boss. The 28-year-old's taciturn nature was portrayed perfectly by a recent interaction with a former colleague on international duty. Japan's fixture with Brazil handed Tanaka a reunion with Lucas Perri, who is out on loan this season with Torino in Serie A. Farke was keen to find out how the pair got on, so asked his midfielder. "Everyone seems to speak about Ao Tanaka," said Farke. "The only one who never seems to speak is Ao Tanaka himself. So we had a short conversation about how it was for him to see Lucas Perri in the game against Brazil. Ao said, 'I said hello...and goodbye. That's it.' So this is how Ao Tanaka is. So he is not a man of many words, but of many skills on the football pitch. And we all love him." His form of late has attracted praise. And numbers back it up. No midfielder in the Premier League presses passing lanes more than Tanaka, who is Leeds' best tackler on Gradient Sports data. What Farke has seen in his midfielder is a level of consistency that was difficult to acquire as he found his feet in the Premier League. "It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship," said Farke. "Last season was his first year in the top league, Premier League level. I think he had also shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of this consistency. And I would also agree that he is finding this during the season. "So it was not always a 10 out of 10 performance, but I think it's important for a player once you're mature that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10. And this is what he's doing. So on perhaps even the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team and also against the ball." Tanaka's tackling prowess is also borne out by data. Gradient say only two players in the Premier League win more tackles per 90 minutes than the Japan international. That's an area in which he has pleased his boss, who still wants more. "Strong in the duels, still sometimes decision-making and in front of the goal he can be a bit calmer," said Farke. "But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment."

sports.title: Rising star to play at World Darts Championship
sports.description: Henry Coates will make his debut at the PDC World Darts Championships in December [PDC] A rising darts star is set to make his dreams a reality by playing at this year's World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace. Henry Coates, 20, secured his place in December's tournament after a breakthrough year which saw him become only the fifth player to win a Professional Darts Corporation (PDC) ranking title without a tour card . Coates, from Matlock, Derbyshire, also narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen during his "incredible" Grand Slam of Darts debut on Saturday. He qualified for the worlds by being a top player on the Challenge Tour Order of Merit rankings , determined by prize money won during the year. "The way that some of the results have gone in my favour means that I'm going to be playing at Ally Pally in December," said Coates. "I'm going to achieve my dream of playing there." Coates narrowly lost 5-4 to former world champion Michael van Gerwen [PDC] Coates, who began playing darts when he was two, secured his qualification for the Grand Slam of Darts by winning his PDC ranking title in the summer. Being from a fifth generation family of butchers, with a shop in Darley Dale, Coates said it was "incredible" to make his debut in the televised competition. The debutant held his own against Van Gerwen but the three-time champion won the deciding leg to clinch a 5-4 win. Despite the close defeat, Coates ended his first Grand Slam on a high with a "better" 5-4 victory over Sweden's Jeffrey de Graaf. "I loved every minute of it. I played so well, even the crowd were chanting my name," he said. He said his phone had been buzzing "non-stop" with messages about his performance during his Grand Slam debut. Parents, Tanya and Nick said watching their son go from playing on a magnetic dartboard while still in nappies to competing against some of the best players in the world "still feels like a dream". His father admitted he still gets nervous watching his son play on the big stage. "I pace about and I have to turn it off because I want him to win and do well," he said. The PDC World Darts Championship, which takes place between 11 December and 3 January, sees a total of 128 players competing to become world champion and claim £1m prize money. This year's event will be held in the Alexandra Palace's Great Hall, for the first time, meaning new attendance records will be set. With his opponents for the tournament still yet to be revealed, Coates hopes a good performance event will take his career to even greater heights. The Dutchman overtook the Mercedes driver, but then slowed down in front of him and, according to the stewards, changed direction several times. It earned both rivals a trip to the stewards, although they ultimately dealt with the incident by issuing a warning. Unlike a reprimand, a warning carries no consequences at all. When Verstappen was asked about the incident during the press conference after qualifying, the Dutchman had little interest in discussing it. Asked what had happened, he simply replied: "Nothing. sports.title: Lakers’ win over Kings fueled by JJ Redick’s halftime speech
sports.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) celebrates a made three from his assist during an NBA basketball game against the Sacramento Kings, Friday November 20th, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES — Walker Kessler picked up three fouls before halftime, and the Lakers went to the locker room down eight to a one-win Sacramento team. JJ Redick had a message for the group and a more pointed one for his starting center. “We got to be tougher, we got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick said of his halftime message. “He definitely lit into me and it was good,” Kessler said. “I needed it. That’s what makes a good coach.” Kessler helped the Lakers erase an 11-point third-quarter deficit, and Quentin Grimes hit a step-back 3-pointer with 56.3 seconds remaining to lift Los Angeles to a 106-104 win over the Kings on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers improved to 14-3 overall and 2-1 in NBA Cup West Group C, picking up their 10th win in 11 games and ending a homestand that had them play three games in a four-day span. Luka Dončić, who led the Lakers with 25 points and eight assists, was asked whether Redick’s halftime talk was more than a talk, which is how Redick put it after the game. “Yeah, I mean, he yells. I’m used to it,” Dončić said. “But it got us all fired up. So sometimes it’s good to hear.” The response took a few possessions. Sacramento stretched its lead to 67-56 early in the third quarter, but Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed two offensive rebounds in the period and threw down a dunk that brought the Lakers within two heading into the fourth. Kessler gave L.A. the lead 18 seconds into the final quarter with his first 3-pointer as a Laker. He later broke an 89-89 tie with a cutting layup off a pass from Collin Sexton, who scored six points in the first five minutes of the quarter. Kessler finished with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks. Matisse Thybulle added 14 points on 4-for-5 shooting from beyond the arc and set up Grimes for the deciding shot. The Lakers led by eight with 4:50 left before the Kings tied it twice. De’Andre Hunter, who scored a game-high 30 points, made a driving bank shot to even the score at 103 before Grimes hit his only 3-pointer of the night. Zach LaVine made one of two free throws to bring Sacramento within two and Kessler missed both of his attempts with 5.3 seconds left which gave the Kings a last chance shot on the final possession from LaVine. LaVine’s potential game-winning 3-pointer hit from the rim at the buzzer that crushed any possibility of sending fans heartbroken. Grimes finished with 13 points and seven assists. Austin Reaves missed his fourth consecutive game with a left heel bruise, and the Lakers will host Utah again Monday at 7 p.m. PT.

technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. technology.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
technology.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.
technology.description: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing : The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows "that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications." technology.title: Army delays detonating "catastrophically hazardous" lead azide amid fear, anger
technology.description: In a swirl of questions, fears, and outrage, the US Army announced Thursday that it would delay a plan to blow up 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide, which would launch toxic gas and lead into the air. A federal appeals court further halted plans later on Thursday with an emergency order. The plume, containing neurotoxic lead, could potentially drift 100 miles north of the Army installation housing it in Middletown, Iowa, according to modeling released by the Army earlier this week. The Army had planned to carry out two controlled detonations, set off simultaneously around noon Friday, to destroy the barrels where they lie, which is in earth-covered concrete containment structures (called earth-covered magazines or ECMs). Prior to the court stay, the Army rescheduled the blast until November 23 to provide more time to communicate about the situation with Iowans, who have reported being unaware of the detonations until earlier this week. "Public communication is essential to public trust," Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said in a post on social media at 7:31 pm ET Thursday . science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers.
